postconditions.description: The result is at least 1, as there is always at least one perfect square number (1) that sums to any positive integer.
The result is at most n, as the sum of perfect square numbers cannot exceed n.

postconditions.expression: all(n % (i * i) == 0 for i in range(1, int(n**0.5) + 1))
postconditions.description: For every integer i in the range from 1 to the integer part of the square root of n, n is divisible by i*i, meaning n can be expressed as a sum of perfect square numbers.

postconditions.expression: result == min(sum(1 for i in range(1, int(n**0.5) + 1) if n % (i * i) == 0) for j in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The result is the minimum number of perfect square numbers that sum to n, where the inner sum counts the number of perfect square numbers needed for each possible sum from 1 to n, and the outer minimum finds the smallest count among them.
